item.title: Neocloud short sellers rack up $6 billion as AI debt fears deepen
item.description: Short sellers betting against US neocloud and data centre companies have made about $6 billion in paper profits this month as AI debt fears trigger a sharp selloff. CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN, Applied Digital and Core Scientific face heavy short interest, highlighting growing concerns over debt-fuelled AI infrastructure spending.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Short sellers betting against US neocloud and data centre companies have accumulated about $6 billion in unrealised profits this month as concerns over debt fuelled AI spending trigger a sharp selloff across the sector, Reuters reported.The pressure has been particularly strong in companies seen as major beneficiaries of the AI infrastructure boom, with investors increasingly questioning whether aggressive data centre expansion can be supported by rising debt.CoreWeave, Nebius face heavy short betsShort interest in CoreWeave, IREN, Nebius Group, Applied Digital and Core Scientific stood between about 20% and 26% of their free floats, according to data analytics firm ORTEX, cited by Reuters.CoreWeave has seen its short interest rise to 23.7% of free float, from 19.6% at the start of October. Short sellers have made nearly $1.7 billion in paper profits from the stock this month after its shares fell almost 30%.Nebius has also attracted heavier bearish bets, with short interest reaching 20% of its free float, compared with 15.4% at the start of the year. Investors betting against the company have made $2.94 billion in paper profits in October, although they remain down $3.33 billion on a year to date basis.Data centre stocks face broader pressureShort sellers of IREN and Applied Digital have together made more than $1.2 billion in paper profits this month, while bearish bets against Core Scientific have generated another $115 million, Reuters reported.Across the five companies, around $17 billion worth of stock is currently sold short, ORTEX said. Borrowing also remains cheap for all five, potentially allowing bearish positions to remain in place.The selling continued on Thursday. CoreWeave and Nebius fell more than 4% in early trading, while IREN dropped 6.1%, Applied Digital declined 3.7% and Core Scientific slipped 2.4%.The moves highlight how quickly sentiment around AI infrastructure stocks can turn when investors begin questioning the economics of rapid, debt backed expansion.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: Yes Bank unlikely to pay AT1 bond coupons despite bond holders demand, sources say
item.description: Yes Bank has announced potential non-payment of coupons on additional tier-1 bonds this fiscal year following a Supreme Court decision that annulled the previous write-off of these bonds. Bondholders are advocating for repayment based on the court's ruling, which emphasizes unsettled dues. Nonetheless, Yes Bank maintains it has ultimate authority over coupon payments, raising concerns about its financial losses impacting these obligations.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's Yes Bank is unlikely to pay coupons due this year on its additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds despite a Supreme Court ruling overturning their write-off during the lender's 2020 rescue, two persons familiar with the matter said.The bank is preparing to seek a review of the ruling, one of the sources told Reuters, while bondholders press for payment of coupons that have remained unpaid since Yes Bank wrote the bonds off six years ago.Last week, India's Supreme Court upheld a 2023 Bombay High Court ruling that set aside Yes Bank's write-off of 84 billion rupees ($886 million) worth of AT1 bonds, in a setback to the lender and regulators that had defended the move.Yes Bank did not respond to an email seeking comment.The sources declined to be named as they were not authorised to speak on the matter.Retail investors holding the bonds said on Thursday they had not received coupon payments due on October 18, three days after the SC ruling.In a letter to Axis Trustee Services Ltd, reviewed by Reuters, investors sought clarity on the status of coupon payments and urged the debenture trustee to intervene. We call upon the Trustee to obtain immediate written confirmation from Yes Bank as to whether this coupon has been paid, cancelled or remains outstanding, bondholders said.They cited the Supreme Court order that payment of annual coupons shall remain unaffected by the outcome of these appeals and must be made in terms of the Information Memoranda. The sources, however, said the bond documentation gives the bank discretion over coupon payments and that the issue can only be considered once the AT1 bonds are reinstated on the bank's balance sheet.The losses the bank accumulated during fiscal years 2020 and 2021 are expected to be fully offset only by fiscal 2028, a third source familiar with the matter told Reuters. This could weigh on the bank's decision to pay coupons on its AT1 bonds, the source added.Yes Bank carries a debit balance of 52.79 billion rupees ($557 million) in its profit and loss account, according to the lender's latest annual report.

item.title: Anthropic IPO stands alone as AI market jitters sideline others
item.description: Anthropic plans to move forward with its initial public offering next month, navigating a challenging IPO landscape. While many companies in the AI field have delayed their public listings due to fluctuating interest rates and significant market instabilities, investors still see potential in Anthropic as a leading tech contender. Concerns are arising from the recent Oura IPO regarding institutional investor interest, emphasizing the heightened scrutiny on AI investment strategies.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A once-robust fall calendar for technology IPOs is down to just Anthropic.The AI lab is pressing ahead to hold its initial public offering as planned in the middle of next month after making its prospectus public as early as late October, people familiar with the matter said, cautioning the plan and the dates are subject to change.Anthropic's planned IPO will test whether its position at the center of the booming AI business, which the company is believed to deem worthy of a potential $1.5 trillion valuation, can overcome a market environment that might typically prompt bankers and deal lawyers to counsel delay. Anthropic is expected to begin marketing its shares to prospective investors during the week of November 9, one of the people said.For live updates on US Markets, click hereOther companies in the artificial intelligence infrastructure and data center sectors have delayed their listings, facing a rise in interest rates that has helped fuel a punishing selloff in shares and bonds of AI operators such as CoreWeave and broader questions about the sustainability of AI spending.The contrast underscores Anthropic's appeal to investors even as concerns about competition from open-source models and AI safety weigh on the sector.Many large investors remain bullish on Anthropic's prospects despite the fall turbulence, viewing the firm as one of the few opportunities to gain exposure to a technology sector that long-term investors cannot afford to ignore. Other issuers are reluctant to compete with Anthropic for institutional investors' attention and capital, two of the people said.Anthropic didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.VALUATIONS COMING UNDER PRESSUREThe AI sector pullback follows a string of IPO delays and withdrawals since September, as market volatility and rising interest rates have made it harder for companies to secure attractive valuations.Switch, a data center operator, and Nscale, an AI infrastructure provider, have pushed their IPO plans back to later this year, people familiar with the matter said, while stressing that plans remain fluid and subject to change. Nscale's delay was partly driven by the need to address comments from SEC staff, one other person said. SoftBank-backed SB Energy has also postponed its listing, Reuters previously reported.Switch, NScale and SB Energy didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.South Korean AI chip startup Elice was among the latest to shelve its listing plans overnight. Blackstone-backed AirTrunk REIT and Nvidia-backed Firmus have also pulled or paused their offerings, Reuters has reported.Oura's recent IPO has added to the caution among prospective issuers. The offering attracted little participation from long-only investors, a person familiar with the matter said, raising concerns about the depth of demand from institutional investors that typically provide a stable base of shareholders for newly listed companies.SCRUTINY ON MULTIPLE FRONTSThe retreat from AI infrastructure listings reflects growing scrutiny of the enormous capital required to build data centers and whether future demand will justify the investment.Recent developments involving CoreWeave have added to concerns about a potential slowdown in AI spending, although some market participants do not expect such a downturn to materialize.Nscale publicly filed its IPO registration statement in September, while Switch submitted its filing confidentially, Reuters reported previously. A confidential filing allows a company to work with regulators on its registration statement before disclosing financial and business details to the public. Companies typically publish the filing ahead of investor roadshows, when they begin marketing shares to prospective investors.
